answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding collateral in identity-specific escrows and linking correlated equivocation across the orchard, inlet, and delta partitions. If k coordinated identities equivocate, the slashing penalty scales as O(k²), so splitting control among more identities increases rather than diversifies exposure. Upon detection, an additional exponential multiplier on capital loss makes a large sybil swarm disproportionately costly, while asymmetric depreciation prevents recovered collateral from restoring its original value.
